feature: Finding why screenshots miss the clipboard on your other Mac
summary: Not fixed, and the cause is not found. On this Mac, captures pasted correctly every time, including real pastes into Chrome, so the next step is a report run on the Mac where it fails.
setup: On the other Mac, with one Photonz running. Copy over the single file Scripts/clipboard-timing/other-mac-report.sh. It needs no permissions, no compiler and no copy of the repo. No app code changed in this task.

try.do: In Terminal there, run: zsh other-mac-report.sh 10
For ten minutes, take screenshots and paste them the way you normally do.
Note any paste that failed, and which app you were pasting into.
Bring back the photonz-clipboard-report file it leaves on the Desktop.

evaluate: Does the report say NO COPY for a screenshot that failed? That points at the shortcut or the capture, not the clipboard.
Does it say REPLACED? Then something else wrote over the picture, and this Mac's loop is a suspect.
Does copying text on this Mac show up when you paste on the other one? If so, Universal Clipboard links them.
Which version of Photonz is on that Mac, and which apps were you pasting into?
rough: Measured on the probe build, not the released 0.23.0: 30 of 30 captures pasted into real Chrome by its own paste command (24, then 6), at once, 1 s and 3 s.
A sandboxed stand-in reader got 15 of 15, about two per kind of read and delay. That rules out sandboxed apps always failing, not a rare failure, and it is still a stand-in.
Those captures were landed by a walk from a saved picture. No capture shortcut was pressed, and region, window and full screen were not tried separately.

Not tested at all: Preview, Notes, Safari, Messages, Mail and Claude need an Accessibility grant this loop does not have; Slack and Teams are not installed. No test covered a long idle, sleep or macOS 26.
The one-released-app run was not done: it needs Photonz Dev quit, and a runner may not quit it.
Chrome pasted the screenshot's FILE, not the PNG data, which the earlier stand-in reader never showed. So a paste into Chrome depends on that file being readable.
Suspect, unconfirmed: macOS's own screenshot shortcuts are off on this Mac but on by default on a fresh one, and macOS's own capture never touches the clipboard. The report prints their state.
Suspect, unconfirmed: Universal Clipboard is live here, each clipboard write is advertised, and the loop writes the clipboard all day. Nothing yet shows the other Mac receives it.
Suspect from reading code only: a full-screen capture on two displays leaves only the last display's picture on the clipboard. This Mac has one display.
